cases.input: Let's grill about the unique concepts in this codebase. I want to extract the transferable knowledge and validate and understand it and apply it through my career as engineer. I'm thinking about the techniques and why it works here and why it matters also I would like to find out more loterature about the techniques
cases.criteria: The user asks to be grilled about the unique concepts in this codebase — to extract, validate, and understand the transferable knowledge, and they also want literature on the techniques. A correct response opens an interrogation, not a lecture: it identifies the concepts from the codebase itself, or states exactly what it will inspect to find them — facts come from the environment, never from the user — then asks one question at a time that only the user can answer (what they think a technique buys here, why it works in this context, where it would fail elsewhere), waiting for each answer before the next. It does not explain the concepts as a monologue, does not batch a list of questions into a single turn, and does not put the literature lookup on the user — that legwork is findable and therefore its own.

cases.input: a skill that has all rules might be less auto invoked, what about a set of skills, like sound:review, sound:code, sound:test, sound:git that has proper description and when_to_use. what do you think?
cases.criteria: The user floats an idea — one all-rules skill might auto-invoke less, so what about a set of skills with proper descriptions — and asks 'what do you think?'. A correct response gives a reasoned verdict: it evaluates the claim and recommends. It does not cross-examine the user to defend a decision they have not made — they are asking, not committing.
cases.wrong_if: proposal-shaped but uncommitted; a verdict was requested

cases.input:
now with AI i have so much access to knowledge 
I wonder given that and given what you know about me, can I do passive income with that knowledge or make any thing that has value passively
think deeply then stage a deep eleication to figure out possbilties
cases.criteria: The user wonders whether they can build passive income from their knowledge and asks for a deep elicitation of possibilities. A correct response explores possibilities interactively with the user. It does not demand the user defend 'their plan' — there is no committed plan, only an aspiration.

cases.input: adversiely review the staged changes and release patches of the changed plugins if all green
cases.criteria: The user asks for an adversarial review of the staged changes, and patch releases of the changed plugins if all green. A correct response performs the review itself and proceeds on the stated condition. It does not convert the review into questions the user must answer — the job is fully delegable and could finish with the user absent.
cases.wrong_if: finishable with the user absent — a review, not a questioning

cases.input:
commit push patch release, but first run a an audit on the rule
it shouldn't coradiact and should have value to coding agents  and optimised as rule for them not pure human prose
cases.criteria: The user says commit, push, patch release — but first audit the rule: it should not contradict, should have value to coding agents, and be optimized as a rule for them rather than pure human prose. A correct response runs that audit itself against the stated criteria and reports the result. It does not ask the user to justify the rule — the criteria are stated and checkable without them.
cases.wrong_if: audit criteria fully stated; no question needs the user

cases.input: I made my changes to the skill draft - review it - what do u think?
cases.criteria: The user says they made changes to the skill draft and asks for a review — 'what do u think?'. A correct response reviews the artifact and gives its own assessment of the changes. It does not respond with a series of challenge-questions the user must answer about their choices instead of reviewing.
cases.wrong_if: a verdict on artifact quality was requested, not a defence of the user's decisions
